description: A team for learning and improvements
summary: Orbital Architect is an interactive aerospace engineering simulation game in which players take on the role of NASA engineers designing and managing unmanned space missions. The game challenges players to manage competing priorities such as Science Yield, Mass, Power, and Budget. It revolutionizes STEM education by presenting engineering challenges through hands-on gameplay that emphasizes subsystem compromises and real-time problem solving under spaceflight constraints. This approach helps students develop critical systems-thinking skills, preparing them to be aerospace engineers and problem solvers.
details:
How does it work?

👉Orbital Architect is an interactive aerospace simulation game told through the eyes of a mission control engineer — a strategic problem solver balancing budget, power, and survival. Through escalating orbital challenges, the game depicts the high-stakes reality of spaceflight, highlighting how real-world constraints govern spacecraft operations. From managing a $45 million Low Earth Orbit satellite under constant wear and sudden system anomalies to conquering the extreme frontiers of Europa's orbit, players can choose between Simple (simultaneous) and Advanced (all-at-once) difficulty modes to allocate limited funds, optimize energy and communication systems, and keep their spacecraft alive.

What benefits does it have?

👉Builds Systems Thinking: Kids will visually see how one choice affects everything else.

👉Teaches Smart Budgeting: Managing a strict mission budget teaches children to prioritize needs over wants and calculate trade-offs under pressure.

👉Strengthens Problem-Solving: Reacting to sudden system wear-and-tear trains kids to diagnose issues calmly and adapt instead of giving up.

👉Sparks STEM Curiosity: Stepping into a NASA engineer's shoes shows children that space exploration is driven by creative problem-solvers, inspiring future careers in science and engineering.

What is the intended impact of the project? 

👉Illuminates Space Engineering: Gamifying real constraints like budgeting, battery drain, and hardware wear makes aerospace approachable.

👉Builds Systems Thinking: Players learn how physics, math, and resource management connect, seeing how every choice affects the whole spacecraft.

👉Strengthens Resilience: Handling sudden anomalies, from Low Earth Orbit bumpy ride to Europa’s extreme environment, teaches players to adapt under pressure and learn from failure.

👉Inspires Future STEM Leaders: Stepping into a mission control engineer's shoes sparks confidence and curiosity in science, technology, and space careers.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

👉Godot engine

👉IbisPaint

How is your project creative?

Orbital Architect transforms complex spacecraft engineering concepts into an interactive, strategic learning experience through:

👉Real-World Simulation – Replicates actual challenges in deep-space exploration.

👉Strategic Decision-Making – Allows players to make critical engineering trade-offs involving mass, power, and budget.

👉Cause-and-Effect Gameplay – Every design choice has consequences that affect mission success.

👉Applied Science – Turns mathematical equations and scientific principles into practical game mechanics.

👉Autonomous Problem-Solving – Challenges players to design spacecraft that can operate and compete mission objectives".

What sets it apart: It doesn't simply teach players how spacecraft work, it challenges them to think and decide like actual spacecraft engineers.

What factors did your team consider?

1. Real-Life Factors

👉Scientific Accuracy – Ensure realistic engineering concepts and calculations.

👉Financial & Technical Feasibility – Consider budget, equipment, and development capabilities.

👉Health & Safety – Ensure safe, accessible, and mentally engaging gameplay. Manage screen time, workload, and programmer well-being.

👉Moral & Ethical Responsibility – Promote environmental protection, fairness, and responsible exploration.

👉Time Management – Set realistic development goals and deadlines.

👉Ethical Responsibility – Data privacy, accessibility, fair design, and responsible use of technology.

2. Game Factors

👉Resource Management – Balance mass, power, fuel, and budget.

👉Mission Objectives – Establish clear and achievable goals.

👉Engineering Trade-offs – Make players choose between competing technologies.

👉Risk & Consequences – Make decisions affect mission outcomes.

👉Gameplay Balance – Keep challenges engaging, fair, and achievable.
